anim_theme_aide: Show only the animations of one topic.
anim_compte: {faites} animations available out of {total} in the original catalogue.
anim_credits: After ClassAction, University of Nebraska-Lincoln Astronomy Education (Apache License 2.0). Remade in Python: checked computations, bilingual interface.
anim_desc_hammerthrower: Illustrates how the movement of a star and its planet about their center of mass compares to a hammer thrower swinging a heavy metal ball.
anim_desc_eclipsingbinarysim: Models the motions of two stars in orbit around each other, and the combined lightcurve they produce. This simulator allows the user to control multiple parameters to see how they affect the lightcurve. Includes several real datasets.
anim_desc_gravalgebra: Shows how the force of gravity would be different if the values used in Newton's law of universal gravitation formula are changed.
anim_desc_lightcurve: Shows how a lightcurve is constructed from observations of an eclipsing binary system.
anim_desc_centerofmass: Shows how the center of mass of two objects changes as their masses change.
anim_desc_solarsystemproperties: Allows one to explore a set of histograms for characteristics like number of satellites, mass, orbital period, etc. for the terrestrial and jovian planets, plus Pluto.
anim_desc_formationtemps: Shows planet formation temperature as a function of distance from the Sun. Also indicates the state (gas or solid) of several substances at the given distance and temperature.
anim_desc_daylightsimulator: Simulation showing daylight and nighttime regions on a flat map of Earth. Daily and yearly motions of the sunlight pattern can be shown.
anim_desc_celestialhorizon: Demonstrates how the celestial sphere and horizon diagram are related.
anim_nom_siderealtimeandhourangledemo: Sidereal Time and Hour Angle Demonstrator
anim_desc_siderealtimeandhourangledemo: Shows how sidereal time and the hour angle of a star are related.
anim_desc_smallangledemo: Shows how small angles can be approximated.
anim_desc_dipperclock: Shows how stars rotate around the North Star over time (both daily and seasonal motions are shown).
anim_desc_heliacalrisingsim: Demonstrates how the day of the year when a star is first visible in the morning (the heliacal rising) depends on the observer's latitude and the star's position on the celestial sphere.
anim_desc_wagonwheel: Demonstrates aliasing through the analogy of a wagon wheel being filmed. For some combinations of frame rates and true rotation speeds the wheel can appear to rotate backwards.
anim_desc_daylighthoursexplorer: Shows the hours of daylight received during the year for an observer at a given latitude. This is an important factor contributing to the seasons.
anim_desc_meridaltdiagram: Shows the geometry for calculating the meridional altitude of objects.
anim_desc_latsim: Shows how an observer's latitude determines the circumpolar, rise and set, and never rise regions in the sky.
anim_desc_seasonsim: Shows how the sun's declination and right ascension change over the course of a year.
anim_desc_transitmovie: Demonstrates the changing declination of the sun with a time-lapse movie, which shows how the shadow of a building changes over the course of a year (simulated here).
anim_desc_altazimuth: Demonstrates the horizon coordinate system, where altitude and azimuth define an object's position in the sky.
anim_desc_zodiac: Shows the sun's position in the sky relative to the background stars (the zodiac constellations) over the course of a year.
anim_desc_longlat: Demonstrates latitude and longitude with an interactive globe, providing an analogy to the celestial and horizon coordinate systems.
anim_desc_radecdemo: Demonstrates the celestial-equatorial (RA/dec) coordinate system, where declination and right ascension define an object's position on the celestial sphere.
anim_desc_sunpaths: Shows how the declination of the sun varies over the course of a year using a horizon diagram.
anim_desc_sunmotions: Models the motions of the sun in the sky using a horizon diagram, demonstrating daily and seasonal changes in the sun's position.
anim_desc_sunsrays: Shows how the sun's most direct rays hit different parts of the earth as the seasons change.
anim_desc_horizon: Shows how the direction of the sun at sunrise or sunset changes over the course of the year.
anim_desc_bigdipper: Demonstrates how the stars of the Big Dipper, which are at various distances from earth, project onto the celestial sphere to give the familiar asterism.
anim_desc_eclipticsimulator: Shows the geometry of the earth and sun over the course of a year, demonstrating how seasons occur. This simulator allows both orbital and celestial sphere representations of the seasonal motions.
anim_desc_celhorcomp: Shows how the rotation of the earth leads to the apparent rotation of the sky, and how celestial sphere and horizon diagram representations of the sky are correlated.
anim_desc_balloon: An animation of coins attached to a balloon, providing an analogy to the expansion of the universe. The coins represent galaxies, which maintain their scale while the space between them grows.
anim_desc_ca_extrasolarplanets_graph: Shows a star and planet in orbit around each other while tracing out the star's radial velocity curve.
anim_nom_ca_extrasolarplanets_starwobble: Influence of Planets on the Sun
anim_desc_ca_extrasolarplanets_starwobbl: Shows the movement of the sun due to the gravitational pull of the planets. The contribution from each planet can be isolated by toggling checkboxes.
anim_desc_pulsarperiodsim: Demonstrates how the movement of a pulsar and planet around their common center of mass affects the timing of pulse arrivals.
anim_desc_radialvelocitydemo: Demonstrates how the spectrum of a star is shifted as it and its planet orbit their common center of mass.
anim_desc_transitsimulator: Demonstrates how a planet passing in front of its parent star can cause dips in the star's lightcurve, potentially leading to the planet's detection.
anim_desc_radialvelocitysimulator: Models the motion of an extrasolar planet and its star around their common center of mass, and the effect this motion has on the star's observed radial velocity.
anim_desc_lookbacktimesim: Shows how the finite speed of light and the great distances to most astronomical objects cause us to observe things as they were in the past.
anim_desc_meltednail: A movie showing the heating and eventual melting of a nail, and the theoretical blackbody curve produced in the process.
anim_desc_spectrum010: Allows one to generate a variety of simulated spectra, depending on factors such as the type of source, luminosity class, spectral type, and individually selected elements.
anim_desc_emspectrum: Surveys the electromagnetic spectrum, showing a typical astronomical image for different wavelengths of light and the kind of instrument that would take such an image.
anim_desc_bbexplorer: Demonstrates how the blackbody spectrum varies with temperature. This explorer also shows how the relative intensities observed through different filters (a 'color index') can give an estimate of temperature.
anim_desc_dopplershift: Shows circular waves expanding from a source. Movement of the source or observer affects the frequency of the waves seen by the observer, demonstrating doppler shift.
anim_desc_filters: Demonstrates how different light sources and filters combine to determine an observed spectrum. This simulator also shows the perceived colors associated with the spectra shown.
anim_desc_hydrogenatom: Models a hydrogen atom and its interactions with light, demonstrating the quantum nature of absorption and emission.
anim_desc_threeviewsspectra: Demonstrates how different spectra can arise from a light bulb (a thermal source) and a cold, thin gas cloud. The spectrometer shows emission, absorption, or continuous spectra based on where the draggable telescope is pointed.
anim_desc_basketball: Shows an illuminated basketball that can be viewed from multiple directions, providing an analogy to moon phases.
anim_desc_eclipsetable: Consists of a table of solar and lunar eclipses, showing the banding that represents the eclipse seasons that occur about twice a year.
anim_desc_fullmoondec: Shows the declination range of the full moon over the course of a year, and the corresponding changes in altitude for a northern hemisphere observer.
anim_desc_lunar_applet: Demonstrates the correspondence between the moon's position in its orbit, its phase, and its position in an observer's sky at different times of day.
anim_desc_lunar_phaser: Shows the appearance of the moon at each of the named moon phases.
anim_desc_mooninc: Demonstrates how the inclination of the moon's orbit precludes eclipses most of the time, leading to distinct eclipse seasons.
anim_desc_moonphases: Shows how the phase of the moon depends on the viewing geometry by allowing the moon to be viewed from the earth, the sun, and an arbitrary point in space.
anim_desc_phasedemonstrator: Demonstrates how planet and moon phases depend on orbital geometry. Users can drag two bodies around to see how the observed appearances change.
anim_nom_positionsdemonstrator: Moon Phases and the Horizon Diagram
anim_desc_positionsdemonstrator: Provides a method of learning the correlation between the phase of the moon, the time of day, and the position of the moon in the sky.
anim_desc_shadowsim: Provides draggable earth and moon discs with shadows, which can be used to demonstrate how the umbral (complete) and penumbral (partial) shadows give rise to different types of eclipses.
anim_desc_synodiclag: Demonstrates the difference between a sidereal and synodic (solar) day, which arises from the earth's revolution around the sun.
anim_desc_tidesim: Shows how the sun, moon, and earth's rotation combine to create tides.
anim_desc_milkywayrotationalvelocity: A plot of the rotational velocity of stars at varying distances from the center of the Milky Way. A draggable cursor allows determining the contained mass implied by the curve.
anim_desc_trafficdensity: The build-up of traffic behind a slow moving tractor provides an analogy to the density wave formation of spiral arms.
anim_desc_antikythera: The Greek astronomical calculator of the 2nd century BC, in 3D: turn the crank and the 33 gears drive the Egyptian calendar, the Sun and the Moon through the zodiac, the Moon phase, the planets of the Cosmos, the Metonic and Saros spirals and their eclipse glyphs. Closed or open machine, exploded levels, exact gear ratios. Adapted from Anticythere3D, by the same author.
anim_desc_orion3d: Like the Big Dipper 3D, for Orion: Betelgeuse, Bellatrix, Meissa, the Belt (Mintaka, Alnilam, Alnitak), Saiph, Rigel and the sword (Hatysa, the Trapezium of M42) at their measured distances, with the Earth, the lines of sight and the figure on the celestial sphere. Face-on we find the constellation; turning it, we see its stars spread from 77 to 400 parsecs. M42 and the Horsehead in place; true colours and a data sheet for each object on hover.
anim_desc_gravityorbits: The Sun, the Earth, the Moon or the space station under gravity, computed step by step: forces and velocities as arrows, paths, grid and measuring tape, gravity that can be turned off, masses that can be changed, bodies to move and velocities to pull. “Model” or to-scale view (where the Earth and the Moon are a single dot), measured periods compared with the true ones, energy conserved, the Moon’s path seen from the Sun. After the PhET simulation “Gravity and Orbits” (University of Colorado Boulder).
anim_desc_venusphases: Shows what Venus looks like through a telescope as the planets go around in their orbits. Compare with the Ptolemaic Phases of Venus simulation.
anim_desc_ptolemaic: Shows what Venus would look like through a telescope if Ptolemy's model was correct. Compare with the other Phases of Venus simulation.
anim_desc_marsorbit: Shows Ptolemy's model for the orbit of Mars.
anim_desc_pathtracer: Demonstrates that the heliocentric and geocentric models are equivalent for predictive purposes when limited to circular orbits. One can watch the same system in motion with different bodies held in fixed position.
anim_desc_retrograde: Demonstrates the retrograde motion of Mars with an annotated animation.
anim_desc_keplers_third: Lets one calculate the period of a planet from its semimajor axis, and vice versa.
anim_desc_synodiccalculator: Lets one calculate the sidereal period of the planet (P) from the synodic period (S), and vice versa.
anim_desc_configurationssimulator: Models the movements of the planets around the sun in a simplified Copernican model of the solar system.
anim_desc_kepler: Models the motion of a hypothetical planet that orbits the sun according to Kepler's laws of motion. This simulator includes controls for investigating each of Kepler's laws.
anim_desc_ellipsedemo: Demonstrates the parameters that define the eccentricity of an ellipse.
anim_desc_stellarmag: Shows how the distance modulus formula combines apparent and absolute magnitudes to give the distance to a star.
anim_desc_stellarvel: Shows how the distance to a star, its doppler shift, and its proper motion allow one to calculate the star's true space velocity.
anim_desc_parallaxdiag: Diagrams the geometry and shows the math involved in determining a star's distance via parallax.
anim_desc_spectroparallax: Demonstrates how the technique of spectroscopic parallax works. Spectral type and luminosity class determine the observed spectrum of a star, from which the star's luminosity can be estimated.
anim_desc_stellarlum: Demonstrates how a star's luminosity depends on its temperature and radius.
anim_desc_lightdetector: Demonstrates the inverse square law of light with a lightbulb and detector. The lightbulb's intensity and the detector's distance can be adjusted to see how they affect the reading. There are two bulbs and detectors to allow side-by-side comparisons.
anim_desc_hrexplorer: Introduces the Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram, a plot showing the relationship between luminosity and temperature for stars.
anim_desc_fusion01: Shows an animated diagram of the proton-proton chain reaction, which is the dominant fusion reaction in the sun's core.
anim_desc_fusion02: Shows an animated diagram of the CNO cycle, which dominates in stars larger than the sun.
anim_desc_telescope10: Demonstrates the properties of a telescope, and how these vary with aperture and eyepiece selection.
anim_desc_buckets: Shows a rainfall and bucket analogy to CCD imaging.
anim_desc_drivingthroughsnow: Shows a snow shower from the perspective of a car driving through it, demonstrating how the snow seems to diverge from some central point (the radiant). Provides an analogy to a meteor shower.
anim_desc_antipodesexplorer: Demonstrates antipodal points, which are points on opposite sides of the Earth from each other.
anim_desc_sunmotionsoverview: Shows the paths of the sun on the celestial sphere.
anim_desc_gravcalc: Allows one to calculate the force of gravity acting on a variety of masses over a range of distances.
anim_desc_earthorbitplot: Shows the orbital period as a function of orbital distance for satellites of Earth.
anim_desc_lunarphasequizzer: Shows the standard orbital view of the Moon, but with the option to hide the Moon's phase, the Moon's position, or the Sun's direction.
anim_desc_snellslaw: Demonstrates Snell's Law, a formula that describes how light is refracted when it moves between different media.
anim_desc_galacticredshift: Demonstrates the redshift of a galaxy due to the expansion of the universe, and the effect this shift has on the galaxy's brightness as observed through various filters.
anim_desc_moonbisector: Demonstrates a method for determining moon phases using planes that bisect the earth and moon.
anim_desc_siderealsolartime: Helps demonstrate the difference between sidereal and solar time.
